# Choose a reading route

[Overview](../README.md) · [Primer](primer.md) · [Evaluation guide](evaluation-guide.md)

These are suggested study sequences, not rankings. Read the mechanism and evaluation boundary together; follow the linked primary paper for the full argument.

<a id="foundations"></a>

## Foundations and boundaries

What is the difference between solving a task and learning something reusable?

1. **[ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models](papers.md#react)** — Identify the fixed reasoning/action loop and its observations.

2. **[Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback](papers.md#self-refine)** — See how an answer can improve while the agent itself stays unchanged.

3. **[Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning](papers.md#reflexion)** — Trace how verbal feedback affects retries, and ask what survives a new task.

4. **[ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners](papers.md#expel)** — Follow the transition from individual trajectories to reusable cross-task insights.

5. **[Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models](papers.md#voyager)** — Compare declarative insights with an executable skill library.

6. **[A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: What, When, How, and Where to Evolve on the Path to Artificial Super Intelligence](papers.md#self-evolving-survey)** — Place the mechanisms in a broader what/when/how taxonomy.


**Study exercise:** Draw two timelines: one for a single task and one spanning several tasks. Mark every state update and every reset.

<a id="memory-skills"></a>

## Memory and skills

How can experience become useful knowledge, a procedure, or a reusable tool?

1. **[ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners](papers.md#expel)** — Start with extracting and reusing experience across tasks.

2. **[Agent Workflow Memory](papers.md#agent-workflow-memory)** — Follow workflow induction from successful trajectories.

3. **[ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory](papers.md#reasoningbank)** — Compare reusable reasoning memories extracted from successes and failures.

4. **[MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory](papers.md#memrl)** — Separate learning a memory utility estimate from updating the reasoning model.

5. **[SkillRL: Evolving Agents via Recursive Skill-Augmented Reinforcement Learning](papers.md#skillrl)** — Contrast external skills with parameter learning and teacher-derived supervision.

6. **[SkillFlow:Benchmarking Lifelong Skill Discovery and Evolution for Autonomous Agents](papers.md#skillflow)** — Examine whether skill use produces measurable benefit.


**Study exercise:** For three methods, write the stored artifact, admission rule, retrieval rule, revision rule, and evidence that reuse helps.

<a id="agent-design"></a>

## Agent design and optimization

Which parts of an agent can be optimized, and who performs that optimization?

1. **[DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines](papers.md#dspy)** — Understand compiling a declarative language-model pipeline with reusable parameters.

2. **[Promptbreeder: Self-Referential Self-Improvement via Prompt Evolution](papers.md#promptbreeder)** — Inspect evolution of prompts and mutation instructions.

3. **[GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning](papers.md#gepa)** — Compare textual feedback with reward-only search.

4. **[Automated Design of Agentic Systems](papers.md#adas)** — Expand the search from prompts to agent implementation code.

5. **[AFlow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation](papers.md#aflow)** — Study search over workflow operators and evaluation-driven selection.

6. **[Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models](papers.md#ace)** — Contrast whole-prompt replacement with incremental context updates.


**Study exercise:** Make an editable/fixed component table. Include proposer, search space, selector, evaluation set, and stopping rule.

<a id="model-learning"></a>

## Learning in model weights

Where does supervision come from when a model helps generate its own training data?

1. **[STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning](papers.md#star)** — Track answer checks, rationale generation, and fine-tuning.

2. **[Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions](papers.md#self-instruct)** — Distinguish generated instruction coverage from verified correctness.

3. **[Reinforced Self-Training (ReST) for Language Modeling](papers.md#rest)** — Examine the generation/filtering/learning cycle and its external reward signal.

4. **[Self-Rewarding Language Models](papers.md#self-rewarding-lms)** — Ask what changes when a model also supplies preference judgments.

5. **[Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning](papers.md#score)** — Separate a learned correction policy from untrained prompting.

6. **[Self-Adapting Language Models](papers.md#seal)** — Study generated self-edits, adaptation rewards, and retention limits.


**Study exercise:** For each loop, label which information is human-provided, pretrained, environment-verified, or model-judged.

<a id="self-play"></a>

## Self-play and curricula

Can a system generate useful challenges for itself?

1. **[Mastering the game of Go without human knowledge](papers.md#alphago-zero)** — Start with a domain whose rules and outcomes provide exact feedback.

2. **[Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data](papers.md#absolute-zero)** — Move from game outcomes to executable reasoning tasks and proposer/solver roles.

3. **[R-Zero: Self-Evolving Reasoning LLM from Zero Data](papers.md#r-zero)** — Inspect a challenger/solver curriculum and its dependence on model-derived signals.

4. **[Self-Challenging Language Model Agents](papers.md#self-challenging-agents)** — Study agent-generated tool-use challenges.

5. **[Agent0: Unleashing Self-Evolving Agents from Zero Data via Tool-Integrated Reasoning](papers.md#agent0)** — Compare curriculum and executor co-development under tool-related objectives.

6. **[Dr. Zero: Self-Evolving Search Agents without Training Data](papers.md#dr-zero)** — Examine self-evolution in search, where external information changes the feedback setting.


**Study exercise:** Explain what “zero data” excludes for each method and what prior information or engineered environment remains.

<a id="recursive-improvement"></a>

## Improving the improver

Does a method change only the solver, or also the process that improves it?

1. **[Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP): Recursively Self-Improving Code Generation](papers.md#stop)** — Identify how generated program improvements can feed back into the improvement procedure.

2. **[Gödel Agent: A Self-Referential Agent Framework for Recursive Self-Improvement](papers.md#godel-agent)** — Inspect self-referential program modification.

3. **[Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents](papers.md#darwin-godel-machine)** — Study archive-based search and empirical selection of self-edits.

4. **[Hyperagents](papers.md#hyperagents)** — Trace which meta-agent components become editable and which outer controls remain fixed.

5. **[ModularRSI: Modular and Generalizable Recursive Harness Self-Improvement](papers.md#modularrsi)** — Inspect modular evolution and frozen downstream evaluation.

6. **[Reflections on Trusting Trust, Revisited: Contaminating Self-Modifying AI Coding Agents with Poisoned Benchmarks](papers.md#trusting-trust-agents)** — Test the assumption that an optimization benchmark is a trustworthy teacher.


**Study exercise:** Draw the solver, proposer, selector, and evaluator separately. Highlight what can change and what evidence would demonstrate improvement of the improver.

<a id="evaluation"></a>

## Evaluation and failure modes

What experiment would convince you that an agent learned something useful?

1. **[When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs](papers.md#self-correction-survey)** — Begin with feedback and fair-comparison pitfalls.

2. **[PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents](papers.md#past-bench)** — Study matched retained-experience controls with fresh sessions.

3. **[Large Language Model Agents Are Not Always Faithful Self-Evolvers](papers.md#experience-faithfulness)** — Distinguish a stored lesson from causal use of that lesson.

4. **[AgentStream: How Well Do Self-Evolving LLM Agents Perform Under Streaming Tasks?](papers.md#agentstream)** — Compare performance under different task-stream compositions.

5. **[GDPevo: Evaluating Agent Self-Evolution on Real Business Tasks](papers.md#gdpevo)** — Inspect training/test rule recombination and task-selection effects.

6. **[Phantom Gains: Auditing Self-Improvement Against a Measured Null](papers.md#phantom-gains)** — Measure a frozen null before interpreting per-problem changes.

7. **[Reflections on Trusting Trust, Revisited: Contaminating Self-Modifying AI Coding Agents with Poisoned Benchmarks](papers.md#trusting-trust-agents)** — Include integrity of the learning signal and persistence of bad updates.


**Study exercise:** Draft a matched frozen baseline, a held-out family split, a budget ledger, and one intervention that could falsify your preferred mechanism.

<a id="continual-learning"></a>

## Continual learning, retention, and drift

Does learning persist when tasks and environments change?

1. **[LifelongAgentBench: Evaluating LLM Agents as Lifelong Learners](papers.md#lifelongagentbench)** — Inspect inter-task dependencies and the limits of replay.

2. **[Building Self-Evolving Agents via Experience-Driven Lifelong Learning: A Framework and Benchmark](papers.md#ell-stulife)** — Separate a proposed lifelong framework from its evaluated baseline protocol.

3. **[LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory](papers.md#longmemeval)** — Study updates, temporal reasoning, and abstention in recalled information.

4. **[AgentStream: How Well Do Self-Evolving LLM Agents Perform Under Streaming Tasks?](papers.md#agentstream)** — Test whether one domain’s experience helps or interferes with another.

5. **[Self-Adapting Language Models](papers.md#seal)** — Examine parameter adaptation and forgetting.

6. **[AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data](papers.md#model-collapse)** — Understand distributional loss under recursive replacement assumptions.

7. **[Is Model Collapse Inevitable? Breaking the Curse of Recursion by Accumulating Real and Synthetic Data](papers.md#accumulating-data-model-collapse)** — Compare replacement with accumulation, retaining the cost and assumption differences.

8. **[Safety in Self-Evolving Agents: A Survey](papers.md#safety-self-evolving-survey)** — Extend retention questions to unsafe influence, repair, and resumed adaptation.


**Study exercise:** Specify separate measures for factual memory, procedural transfer, backward retention, cost, and safety drift. Do not collapse them into one score.
